memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Before our eyes the Lord sent signs and wonders—great and terrible—on Egypt and Pharaoh and his whole household. But he brought us out from there to bring us in and give us the land he promised on oath to our ancestors. The Lord commanded us to obey all these decrees and to fear the Lord our God, so that we might always prosper and be kept alive, as is the case today. - Deut 6:22-24 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The story continues with the reason behind the rescue. God did not simply bring Israel out of Egypt; He brought them out in order to bring them in — into the good land, into a life of relationship and blessing with Him. Salvation was never just about escaping slavery; it was about entering into all that God had prepared. He rescues His people for a purpose: that they might truly live in fellowship with Him.

This "out of" and "into" pattern runs all through Scripture. God does not merely deliver us from something; He delivers us to something. And notice the purpose of the commands: they were given "for our good always," to keep His people alive and flourishing. God's instructions were never meant to crush life but to guard and nurture it. Obedience was the pathway into the fullness God intended.

The same is gloriously true for us in Christ. God brought us out of the slavery of sin and death, but not merely to leave us wandering. He brought us out to bring us in — into His family, His kingdom, His eternal life (Col 1:13). And His commands are still for our good, given by a Father who loves us. When you feel that following God is costly, remember: He rescued you for life, and His ways lead to flourishing. You have been brought out so that you might be brought in.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Do I see salvation only as escape, or also as being brought into something good?
- What is God calling me "into" that I have not fully stepped into?
- How does knowing God's commands are "for my good" change how I obey?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You for not only rescuing me from sin but bringing me into Your family and life. Help me to see that Your commands are for my good, and to walk in the fullness You have prepared for me in Christ. Amen.
